Tosafot on Bava Batra 75b:13:1.hebrew: אחזה בטלפה - פריב"א דמסירה בעינן מיד ליד, ומייתי ראיה מפ"ק דב"מ (דף ח: ושם) דאמר: "מאי לשון מסירה? כאדם שמוסר דבר לחבירו". ואמר נמי התם: "מסירה מחבירו קנה במציאה, ובנכסי הגר לא קנה, דמאן מסר ליה למיקני?" משמע דבעינן מסירה מיד ליד. ואין נראה, דהא קתני הכא "אחזה בטלפה", משמע דבעצמו אחזה. ורבינו שמואל פירש נמי "אחזה בטלפה" במצות המוכר. ועוד דאמר לקמן גבי מסירה: כל היכא דאמר ליה "לך חזק וקני" — כ"ע ל"פ דקנה. ואי בעינן מסירה מיד ליד, לא הו"ל למימר "לך חזק וקני", אלא "תא חזק וקני". והאי דאמר בבבא מציעא (שם) "כאדם המוסר דבר לחבירו", היינו שאומר לו "לך חזק וקני". והא דאמר במציאה ונכסי הגר "מאן מסר ליה", היינו: מי יאמר לו "לך חזק וקני", דליקני באחיזה בעלמא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 75b:13:1.english: He grasped it by its hoof - Pirev"a [i.e., Rabbi Yitzchak ben Asher, the Riva] [held] that for mesirah we require [transfer] from hand to hand, and he brings proof from the first chapter of Bava Metzia (8b, there), which says: "What is the meaning of the term mesirah? Like a person who hands something over to his fellow." And it also says there: "[If one acquires] by mesirah from his fellow, he acquires in the case of a found item; but in the case of a convert's property he does not acquire, for who handed it over to him to acquire?" This implies that we require mesirah from hand to hand. But this does not seem right, for the Mishnah here teaches "he grasped it by its hoof," which implies that he grasped it himself. And Rabbeinu Shmuel also explained "he grasped it by its hoof" [as being done] at the seller's command. Furthermore, [the Gemara] says later regarding mesirah: Wherever he said to him, "Go, take possession and acquire," everyone agrees that he acquires. But if we required mesirah from hand to hand, he should not have said "Go, take possession and acquire," but rather "Come, take possession and acquire." And as for what [the Gemara] says in Bava Metzia (there), "like a person who hands something over to his fellow," this refers to his saying to him, "Go, take possession and acquire." And as for what it says regarding a found item and a convert's property, "who handed it over to him?", this means: who would say to him "Go, take possession and acquire," such that he would acquire by mere grasping.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 75b:14:1.hebrew: אע"ג דעקרה יד ורגל בדוכתה קיימא - וא"ת: אמאי נקט "מלא קומתה", כיון דסגי בעקירת שתי ידים ושתי רגלים? ויש לומר: דעקירת ידיה ורגליה קרי "מלא קומתה":
Tosafot on Bava Batra 75b:14:1.english: Even though she lifted a hand and a foot, she still stands in her place - And if you ask: Why did [the baraita] say "her full height," when lifting two hands and two feet is sufficient? One can answer: The lifting of her hands and her feet is called "her full height."

Tosafot on Bava Batra 75b:9:1.hebrew: טפף גינאות - פי' גינות שוות שבנויות בנין שוה, שאין תוספת ומגרעת בזה ובזה, כמו "הלוך וטפוף תלכנה" (ישעיהו ג׳:ט״ז), וכמו (יומא דף מח.): מדה לא מחוקה ולא גדושה שנקראת טפופה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 75b:9:1.english: Tafaf ginaot - Explanation: [It means] equal gardens that are built with an equal structure, with no addition or subtraction in this one or that one, like "walking and taking tiny steps (tafof) they go" (Isaiah 3:16), and like (Yoma 48a): a measure that is neither leveled off nor heaped, which is called tefufah:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 75b:9:2.hebrew: קפל מגדלין - קפל הן עמודין שוין למגדלין ובנין גבוה, כדאמר באגדת ויקרא: "קפלאות של ברזל". מה עמודים — קפלאות מלמעלה ובסיסאות מלמטה, והן באמצע; כך פרשיות נדרשות לפניהם ולאחריהם:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 75b:9:2.english: A kefel of towers - Kefel refers to columns that are level with towers and a tall building, as it says in the Aggadah of Vayikra [Rabbah]: "Iron kaflaot." Just as with columns, the kaflaot [capitals] are above and the bases are below, and they [the columns] are in the middle; so too, passages are expounded in relation to what precedes them and what follows them.
